# CVForge — LLM Context

## Overview
Next.js 16 App Router for an enterprise frontend.
Connects to an OpenAPI 3.1 backend CVForge API via a typed
client. Lean functional architecture — DDD + Hexagonal modules, no Redux.

Full rules: see AGENTS.md. Architecture: see docs/architecture/00_index.md.
Doc index: docs/README.md.

## Tech Stack
- Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19
- TypeScript (strict mode)
- TanStack Query (server state)
- Zustand (client state)
- react-hook-form + @hookform/resolvers + Zod (forms + validation)
- googleapis (Google Drive API v3 — storage)
- Tailwind CSS v4 (styling, CSS-variable theming)
- Vitest + React Testing Library (testing)
- pnpm (package manager)

## Architecture
- Bounded Contexts: (back-office) and (front-office) route groups under app/[lang]/
- Modular: src/modules/<name>/ with domain/infrastructure/presentation layers
- Public API pattern: modules expose only index.ts barrel
- State: TanStack Query for server data, Zustand for client/session state
- SSR for optimization only — no business logic in the server layer

## Key Files
- src/core/query/ — TanStack Query provider
- src/core/providers.tsx — client provider composition
- src/auth.ts — Auth.js v5 config (Google OAuth + ALLOWED_EMAILS gate)
- src/modules/cv/ — canonical module (CvData schema, Drive repository, editor)

## Module Structure
Each module: domain/ (entities, interfaces, use-cases) → infrastructure/ (repos,
mappers) → presentation/ (components, hooks, state/*.store.ts) → index.ts

## Commands
- pnpm dev — development server (Turbopack)
- pnpm test — unit tests
- pnpm test:coverage — tests with coverage
- pnpm lint — ESLint + Prettier check
- pnpm build — production build
- pnpm type-check — TypeScript check

## Documentation
- docs/README.md — central index
- docs/architecture/00_index.md — architecture hub
- docs/guides/001_branching-and-releases.md — develop/main branching, releases, hotfixes, stacked PRs
